details.description: Llama 3.2 3B Instruct is a 3.21-billion-parameter, instruction-tuned text model in Meta's Llama 3.2 family, released September 25, 2024. Meta pretrained it on up to 9 trillion tokens and instruction-tuned it for multilingual assistant-style chat, agentic knowledge retrieval and summarization, and mobile or on-device AI writing assistants. Amazon Bedrock's model card lists this model's lifecycle as Legacy, with a listed EOL date of July 7, 2026 that has already passed as of this research date.
advantages: Meta reports the model scores 77.7% exact match on GSM8K (chain-of-thought) math reasoning and 78.6% accuracy on ARC-Challenge.
Officially supports 8 languages: English, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Hindi, Spanish, and Thai, per Meta's model card.
Sized for on-device and mobile deployment as a lightweight multilingual assistant, per Meta's model card.
disadvantages: Scores lower than larger Llama models on the same benchmark suite (63.4% MMLU vs 69.4% for Llama 3.1 8B Instruct), per Meta's model card.
Text-only; no image, audio, or video input or output, per Meta's model card.
Knowledge cutoff of December 2023, per Meta's model card.
Amazon Bedrock's model card lists this model's lifecycle as Legacy, with a listed EOL date of July 7, 2026 that has already passed as of this research date (2026-09-24).
use_cases: Mobile and on-device AI writing assistants

sources.title: Llama 3.2: Revolutionizing edge AI and vision with open, customizable models

notes: Catalog's max_input_tokens/max_output_tokens (16384) are lower than the 128K context / 4K max output that Meta's model card and AWS Bedrock both state for this model; kept the catalog's figures per instructions. Amazon Bedrock's own model card (fetched 2026-09-24) lists lifecycle as Legacy with Model EOL date July 7, 2026, already past as of this research date. The GitHub llama3_2 MODEL_CARD.md's own 'Model Release Date' field says Oct 24, 2024, not Sept 25, 2024; Meta's Sept 25, 2024 announcement post confirms Sept 25 is correct, so that source was added. The 69.4% Llama 3.1 8B Instruct MMLU comparison figure is on Llama 3.1's own model card, not one previously listed, so that source was added too.
